$comment: Every difference between text.json and the base witness G, and every letter difference of the other witnesses from text.json, classified. check.py fails on an unlisted difference or an entry that no longer matches. Classes: orthographic (spelling or the printing of a junction; not a reading), variant (another reading in a tradition's text), recension (the Mādhyandina recension differs), witness-error (a slip of the digital witness, with the evidence), review (textual verification required against a printed edition).

corrections.reason: G keys the avagraha after the r (याथातथ्यतोर् ऽथान्); the word is यथातथ्यतः + अर्थान्, written याथातथ्यतोऽर्थान् by every other witness. The letters are unchanged.
A missing space in G; उ is a separate particle (AS, K, Mv, VD).

variants.note: The Mādhyandina witness writes the nasal as ं with ँ (इदंँ); the Kāṇva witnesses write इदं / इदँ. Spelling of one nasal, not a reading.
Madhva’s text spells the nasal before s as ग्ं (the Taittirīya convention). Same word, शतं.
The Mādhyandina witness doubles y after r (असुर्य्या), a common Vedic spelling of असुर्या.
The Mādhyandina recension (VS 40.3) has no ते: ‘asuryā nāma lokāḥ’. Kāṇva witnesses G, AS, K, Mv, VD all read ते.
VS 40.3 (Mādhyandina) reads ‘pretyāpi gacchanti’ (‘go, even after death’) where every Kāṇva witness reads ‘pretyābhigacchanti’ (‘go to them after death’).

The Kāṇva Saṃhitā witness reads अर्शत् (arśat). Mahīdhara, on VS 40.4, also reads अर्शत् and derives it from रिश् ‘to hurt’ (‘not perishing’); the accented Mādhyandina witness M and all Upaniṣad witnesses (G, AS, Mv, VD) read अर्षत् (arṣat), which Śaṅkara glosses ‘गतम्’ (‘gone’, from ऋष्). The edition keeps अर्षत् and shows both readings on the mantra page.

Madhva’s text reads तन्नेजति (tan nejati) for तन्नैजति, and his bhāṣya repeats it: «तत् स्वयं नेजति». The sense is the same (‘it does not move’); na + ejati regularly gives naijati, so nejati is recorded as the reading of Madhva’s text, not adopted.

Madhva’s text omits अस्य: ‘tad u sarvasya bāhyataḥ’ (‘it is outside of all’). Every other witness, Kāṇva and Mādhyandina, has सर्वस्यास्य (‘of all this’). Not verified against a printed text of Madhva’s bhāṣya.

Vedānta Deśika’s text reads ‘tad u naijati’ (‘and yet it does not move’) for ‘tan naijati’, and his bhāṣya quotes it so: «तदु नैजति - तदेव वस्तुवृत्त्या न कम्पते». A reading of the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition, recorded and not adopted.
Advaita Sharada prints the junction in hiatus (भूतानि आत्मन्येव) as a reading aid; with sandhi it is भूतान्यात्मन्येव. Not a reading.

The Saṃhitā witnesses (K and M) read आत्मन्नेव = ātman eva, the Vedic locative without ending (‘in the self’); the Upaniṣad witnesses read आत्मन्येव = ātmani eva, the classical locative. Same meaning, older form in the Saṃhitā.
As K: the endingless Vedic locative ātman.
VS 40.6 (Mādhyandina) reads ‘tato na vi cikitsati’ (‘then he does not doubt’); Mahīdhara: «न विचिकित्सति न संशेते». Every Kāṇva witness reads ‘na vijugupsate’ (‘does not shrink away / hate’).
The same Mādhyandina reading: active ending -ti (cikitsati) against the middle -te (jugupsate).
Printed in hiatus as in AS. Not a reading.
Printed in hiatus as a reading aid. Not a reading.
The Saṃhitā witnesses write यस्मिन्त्सर्वाणि: a t inserted between final n and initial s, an optional junction of the Vedic recitation. Same words.
As K.
Printed in hiatus. Not a reading.
Visarga before ś written as ś (कश्शोक), a South Indian spelling of कः शोक.
Deśika’s mūla as keyed reads अस्राविरँ (asrāviram); every other witness reads अस्नाविरम् (‘without sinews’). Probably a slip of the digital text (स्न / स्र); Deśika’s bhāṣya would settle it.
Visarga before s written as s (परिभूस्स्वयम्भूः). Spelling only.
Visarga before s written as s. Spelling only.
Printed in hiatus (ये अविद्याम्) where the recited text has येऽविद्याम्. Not a reading.
Printed in hiatus. Not a reading.

The Kāṇva Saṃhitā witness reads अविद्याया (avidyāyā) at the end of the line, but विद्यया in the same line: an inconsistency within the witness. The Mādhyandina recension (VS 40.13) reads विद्याया … अविद्यायाः throughout. Textual verification required against a printed Kāṇva Saṃhitā; the edition keeps the reading of every Upaniṣad witness, अविद्यया.

VS 40.13 (Mādhyandina) reads विद्यायाः … अविद्यायाः (‘than knowledge … than ignorance’, ablative) where the Kāṇva Upaniṣad reads विद्यया … अविद्यया (‘by knowledge … by ignorance’, instrumental). A real difference of construction.
The Mādhyandina witness keeps the hiatus after the dropped visarga (विद्याया॑ऽअ॒न्यत्).
The second ablative of VS 40.13; see the first entry for this mantra.
The visarga of the Mādhyandina ablative अविद्यायाः.
Printed in hiatus. Not a reading.
Printed in hiatus. Not a reading.
Deśika’s mūla as keyed reads व्याचचक्षिरे; his bhāṣya on this mantra quotes «ये नस्तद्विचचक्षिरे», as every other witness reads. A slip of the digital mūla.
Visarga before s written as s. Spelling only.
As in mantra 10: the keyed mūla has व्याचचक्षिरे for विचचक्षिरे.

Madhva’s text as keyed lacks the second च (‘sambhūtiṃ ca vināśaṃ yas tad’), which leaves the line a syllable short of the anuṣṭubh. Probably a slip of the digital text; not verified against a printed Madhva bhāṣya.

VS 40.17 (Mādhyandina) has only the first line of this mantra and continues ‘yo ’sāv āditye puruṣaḥ so ’sāv aham | om khaṃ brahma’ (‘the person who is in the sun, that I am. Om, Brahman is space’). The Kāṇva prayer to Pūṣan (15b–16a) is not in it.
Part of the Mādhyandina VS 40.17 (see above).
Part of the Mādhyandina VS 40.17 (see above).
Part of the Mādhyandina VS 40.17 (see above).
Part of the Mādhyandina VS 40.17 (see above): it has no ‘satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye’.
AS, Mv (and K) apply sandhi across the half-line (तेजो यत्ते); G pauses after तेजः. The same words; a matter of where the recitation pauses.

variants.reading: तेजो यत्ते रूपे कल्याणतमं तत्ते पश्यामि
variants.note: The Kāṇva Saṃhitā witness as keyed lacks ‘pūṣann ekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha’ and begins the mantra at तेजो. Every Upaniṣad witness, and Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.15.1 where the same verse occurs, has the full text. Textual verification required against a printed Kāṇva Saṃhitā; whether the omission is the witness’s or the recension’s cannot be decided from the materials available.
Sandhi across the half-line, as AS.
The Kāṇva Saṃhitā witness reads रूपे (‘in the form’) for रूपं; every Upaniṣad witness and BU 5.15.1 read रूपं. Probably a slip of the keyed text; textual verification required.
Sandhi across the half-line, as AS.
Visarga before s written as s. Spelling only.

variants.reading: क्रतो स्मर क्लिबे स्मर कृतं स्मर
variants.note: VS 40.15 (Mādhyandina) reads ‘om krato smara | klibe smara | kṛtaṃ smara’: klibe in place of the repeated ‘kṛtaṃ smara krato smara’ of the Kāṇva text. Mahīdhara takes klibe as a Vedic form of klṛp, ‘the world that is fashioned [for enjoyment]’: «कल्प्यते भोगायेति क्लृप् लोकः तस्मै स्मर».
Part of the same Mādhyandina reading.

variants.reading: ॐ क्रतो स्मर कृतं स्मर ॐ क्रतो स्मर
variants.note: Madhva’s text repeats ॐ before the second ‘krato smara’.
The keyed mūla of Deśika has भस्मान्ँत (a misplaced nasal sign) for भस्मान्तँ.
Same slip.
